paper_metadata.title: A New Initial Distribution for Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks to Load Probability Distributions

summary: This paper proposes a label-replacement method to build qGAN initial distributions using only single-qubit gates, achieving depth d=1 for the initial circuit and an interpretation as d=0 initial weights. In 3-qubit Qiskit simulations over 10 runs, the proposed method attains relative entropy 0.00163 for log-normal targets (better than uniform 0.07702 and normal 0.01320), 0.03931 for triangular targets (better than uniform 0.08249 but worse than normal 0.00289), and 0.11749 for bimodal targets (better than uniform 0.16386 but worse than normal 0.00846).

experiments.description: Simulation study of qGAN training for loading target probability distributions using different initial distributions (proposed label-replacement initial distribution, uniform initial distribution, and normal initial distribution) on 3-qubit quantum generators with varying repetition depth k=1,2,3.

algorithm.variant: qGAN generator training with label-replacement initial distribution
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized Ry layers with interleaved CZ gates; initial distribution circuit uses single-qubit Ry gates or H gates
algorithm.parameter_initialization: generator initial weights randomly sampled from uniform [-10^-1, 10^-1]; proposed initial distribution parameters set from target distribution via label replacement

problem_formulation.encoding_details: probability distributions discretized into 8 points for 3 qubits; generator outputs measurement probabilities over computational basis states
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize relative entropy H(P|Q) between target distribution and generated distribution during adversarial training

problem_instance.description: Learning and loading target probability distributions for qGAN-based state preparation in the context of quantum expectation estimation / finance

dataset_specification.description: target distributions: log-normal (mu=1, sigma=1), triangular (l=0, u=7, m=2), bimodal (mixture of Gaussians with mu1=0.5, sigma1=1 and mu2=3.5, sigma2=0.5); discretized to 8 points

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: samples from each target distribution were sampled 2000 times and discretized by 8 points
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: ten independent training runs for each initial distribution and each target distribution; performance measured by relative entropy (mean, standard deviation, minimum)

implementation_details.classical_solver: Pytorch discriminator; AMSGRAD optimizer; qiskit simulation
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical label replacement used to construct initial distributions; target distributions sampled and discretized
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: relative entropy computation and selection of lowest-entropy generated distributions

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum expectation estimation using amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a general claim about the quantum expectation estimation algorithm, not an empirical runtime measurement in this paper.

speedup_claims.conditions: for log-normal, triangular, and bimodal target distributions; 3-qubit simulations; k=1,2,3; measured by relative entropy over 10 runs
speedup_claims.caveats: Improvement is in relative entropy, not runtime. For bimodal k=3, the mean relative entropy is worse than uniform, though minimum is better.

speedup_claims.factor: better than normal initial distribution for log-normal target
speedup_claims.conditions: log-normal target distribution; 3-qubit simulations; k=1,2,3; measured by relative entropy over 10 runs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the proposed method outperforms the normal initial distribution for log-normal in both mean and minimum relative entropy. For triangular and bimodal, normal is better in mean relative entropy.

speedup_claims.conditions: initial distribution generation via label replacement and/or as initial weights
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a circuit-depth/scalability claim, not a measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: qGAN state preparation intended to support quantum expectation estimation with O(1/epsilon) oracle queries; initial distribution circuit depth d=1 or d=0
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo expectation estimation requires O(1/epsilon^2) simulations

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Shallow qGAN state-preparation circuits with 3 qubits; initial distribution circuit depth d=1 (and d=0 interpretation), simulated in Qiskit.
limiting_factors: No hardware execution on a real quantum device
Classical baselines (normal initial distribution) outperform the proposed method for triangular and bimodal targets on mean relative entropy
The paper's claimed benefit is improved qGAN initialization, not end-to-end quantum advantage
qGAN training remains hybrid and data-loading/classical preprocessing is substantial

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper says the quantum computer was simulated with qiskit on a classical computer and no real QPU was used.
num_qubits inferred from the 3-qubit circuits shown and discussed in the paper.
circuit_depth reported for the initial distribution circuit; the paper also states the proposed initial distribution can be implemented at depth d=0 as initial weights.
The paper reports simulation-only results and does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.

For log-normal targets, the proposed method beats the uniform baseline and also the normal baseline in mean/min relative entropy, but this is an initialization-quality result on a toy 3-qubit simulator, not a system-level advantage.
